scope: OSRAM readout research only; structure lane; no implementation or training
status: 10 mechanism-level implementation candidates, not 10 validated improvements; two-slot shortfall explicitly retained

common_contract.inputs: Current Local256, Base512 and three Gap512 forward reads only, availability, valid-utterance/history mask. No raw past utterances, backward half, labels or external support set.
common_contract.head_tokens: Project Local to d=64 or 128; reshape each active history role as the real 8x64 heads and attach role/head identity. Identity travels with a token under permutations. Legal availability leaves 9/17/25 active tokens.
common_contract.role_tokens: Project entire Local and each entire active 512-d role separately. At least one observed modality implies 2/3/4 active roles including Local.
common_contract.output: Zero-initialized linear residual bridge writes only the original Flat adapter inputs. Keep original Local skip, emotion_adapter/norm, task head and task loss. Explicit per-card write scope overrides a generic all-token bridge.
common_contract.mask: Use where to remove inactive values before any projection; compact valid tokens before normalization, graph construction or solvers; scatter corrections only to their original active coordinates. Padding, first valid utterance/no prior history and ablated-history rows bypass the core with exact identity. Do not identify history absence merely by accidental content zeros when an explicit mask is available.
common_contract.state: All graph, simplex, recurrent and inference states reset at each readout. Static incidence/permutation templates indexed by availability are not new historical memory.
common_contract.claim_limit: Each graph/latent-state assumption is a testable inductive bias, not a discovered semantic structure. Source equations and author code were read; source repositories were not installed or executed. No performance promise; no automatic new auxiliary loss.
implementation_checks: All legal availability patterns and no-history exact bypass
Inactive NaN/large values cannot affect outputs or gradients
Finite forward/backward and task-gradient connectivity after bridge opens
Mechanism-specific algebraic checks in cards; no additional generic review round

cards.title: Learning Structured Text Representations
cards.domain: Document representation; includes text sentiment tasks but is neither MSA nor MERC
cards.code_provenance: Author repository README identifies Liu and Lapata's paper; get_structure/_getDep/_getMatrixTree, lines 53-97 read directly. Parent-child bilinear scores, root scores, first-row Laplacian replacement and inverse-based marginals are present.
cards.previous_status: docs/osram_next40_supplement.json screen_nonprojective_tree_marginal_readout was pending because single-parent prior and broad-family novelty were unproven.
cards.resolution: Latest rule permits a related family with a distinct complete core. Define an explicitly latent nonprojective rooted tree over current evidence heads, not a syntactic parse or historical time chain. Single-parent support remains a declared hypothesis rather than an acceptance claim about data.
computation_graph: Build 9/17/25 compact identity-bearing evidence tokens; split learned structure/content projections.

Compute off-diagonal directed arc scores and a virtual-root score for each node. Subtract each child's maximum across its candidate parents including virtual root before exponentiation; every tree uses exactly one incoming option per child.

Form weighted in-degree Laplacian, replace its first row by root weights, solve the matrix system and obtain root/arc marginals using the source Matrix-Tree identities. Exactly one selected root and a spanning nonprojective tree define the structure distribution.

For each token aggregate parent content, child content and virtual-root content with the globally coupled marginals, concatenate its original content and pass through the source-style content update. Repeat a second structure/content block if fixed at design time, then scatter zero-bridge corrections to Local and active history.
cards.substantive_difference: All edge weights are marginals of one globally normalized acyclic single-root tree distribution. EGT/dual attention have independently normalized edges or learned edge states, and PPGN composes pair tensors without a tree partition function. Not merely a softmax replacement: scoring, root partition, constrained marginals and bidirectional content update form the block.
cards.mask_empty: Compact before the determinant/solve; never retain dummy zero-degree nodes. Empty-history bypass is external. If a unit check calls the core with one token, root marginal=1 and arc matrix=0.
cards.risk: Tree prior can suppress genuine multi-parent interactions. Conditioning can become poor; use float64 small solves, finite checks and explicit failure on singularity, not silent inverse fallback. Original source uses old TensorFlow and unstabilized exp/inverse. Do not claim syntactic or causal interpretability.
mechanism_checks: Root marginals sum to one
Root plus incoming-arc marginal equals one per node
Tiny 2-4 node enumerated-tree marginals agree with matrix formula
Gradcheck stabilized solve away from singularities
cards.benefit_hypothesis: A globally consistent latent dependency scaffold may organize mutually dependent evidence beyond independent attention; improvement unverified.

cards.title: SparseMAP: Differentiable Sparse Structured Inference
cards.domain: Structured prediction and latent computational graphs
cards.paper_read: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/niculae18a/niculae18a.pdf; sections 3.1-3.3, active-set algorithm and support Jacobian
cards.code_provenance: Author repository; read _BaseSparseMarginals.forward/_d_vbar/backward (support M and inverse_A), and TreeSparseMarginals as a concrete factor example. Role partitions below are a new factor instantiation, not a source-provided partition layer.
cards.previous_status: screen_sparsemap_not_additional_count pending: lacked a legal structure separate from budget-QP/OT.
cards.resolution: Use equivalence-relation partitions of the whole active role set. This is neither a subset budget nor balanced transport nor the MatrixTree tree space. A partition encodes which roles should share a temporary evidence group; no group labels are supervised.
computation_graph: Use 2/3/4 full role tokens with Local and role identity. Enumerate all Bell(n)=2/5/15 set partitions as fixed combinatorial templates.

For each partition create a binary off-diagonal co-membership feature column M[:,partition]; every column obeys reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity by construction. Predict pair affinities eta from the current projected roles.

Solve max_{p in simplex} eta^T M p - 0.5 ||M p||^2 using a finite active set and exact enumerated MAP oracle. Differentiate the unique marginal u=M p via the support KKT system, as in SparseMAP; do not regularize ||p||^2 and call it the same algorithm.

Reconstitute a symmetric co-membership matrix U with unit diagonal. Apply receiver-conditioned within-group messages weighted by U, normalize by its row mass, and update each role. A second independently parameterized inference/message block can revise grouping from the updated role content. Decode only original active role coordinates.
Use marginal U for the readout, not an arbitrary nonlinear mixture of partition-specific features: p can be nonunique even when U is unique.
cards.substantive_difference: The equivalence-relation marginal polytope globally couples three-way transitivity and variable group count. OTKE matches to fixed supports, Slot uses soft per-slot responsibilities, EA optimizes an unconstrained summary, and DEQ solves a learned fixed point. This is a new structure space plus constrained graph computation, not changing one existing solver.
cards.mask_empty: Enumerate only active roles; no inactive role participates as a singleton. No-history bypass external; singleton core returns U=[1]. Keep deterministic partition order and deterministic tie policy.
cards.risk: Partition decomposition is nonunique and KKT bases can be affinely dependent. Maintain affinely independent active columns or use the mathematically correct reduced-space pseudoinverse; do not use unconstrained softmax as fallback. Transition surfaces are only almost-everywhere differentiable. With two roles it reduces to one bounded affinity, so larger-mask cases carry the main high-order test. Old AD3/PyTorch 0.2 code is reference, not a dependency request.
mechanism_checks: n=3 partition count=5 and n=4 count=15
All enumerated hard matrices are equivalence relations
KKT residual and primal feasibility
Interior-support finite differences; check ties separately
Never consume nonunique p downstream
cards.benefit_hypothesis: Globally compatible soft grouping may prevent inconsistent independent role pair decisions; benefit is not established.

cards.title: Janossy Pooling: Learning Deep Permutation-Invariant Functions for Variable-Size Inputs
cards.domain: Set functions, arithmetic and graph learning
cards.paper_read: https://arxiv.org/html/1811.01900; Definition 2.1 equation 3, sections 2.2-2.3; paper directly links the author repository
cards.code_provenance: Author arithmetic implementation TextModels.forward uses final LSTM/GRU state; model source read. Paper's exact permutation average is used instead of its costly-set sampling approximation.
cards.previous_status: screen_janossy_exact_role_symmetrization pending due broad-direction proximity and unverified need for invariance.
cards.resolution: Invariance is to enumeration of identity-bearing records, not swapping Base with Gap semantics. Retain role embeddings inside every permuted token. The finite four-role maximum makes exact averaging feasible without artificial head order.
computation_graph: Encode full active Local/Base/Gap roles with their fixed role identity into d=64 tokens.
Enumerate all n! token orders, at most24 under the legal availability contract. For each order run the same LSTM from a fresh zero hidden/cell state, consuming every token exactly once.

Average final hidden states across all permutations before any shared output decoder. For each original role concatenate its own encoding, pooled Janossy result and Local condition, then zero-bridge decode to the original role coordinates.
cards.substantive_difference: Exact group averaging of noncommutative recurrent whole-set compositions is not RRN's graph message recurrence, MAC's learned control/read/write, or FSPool's per-feature sorting. Retain all orders and nonlinear recurrent composition; a single chosen order or sum-pool plus MLP would not be this candidate.
cards.mask_empty: Drop inactive roles before permutations; do not permute padding. Original role identities survive permutation. External no-history bypass. For one role, there is one permutation.
cards.risk: Exact averaging adds up to24 short LSTM evaluations. It removes only list order and may be unnecessary because Flat already has explicit semantic slots. No claim of permutation invariance to changing role labels, and no time interpretation for the LSTM step.
mechanism_checks: All n! permutations are unique
Reordering input records together with their identities leaves pooled result unchanged
A nonlinear LSTM is present before averaging
No recurrent state is reused across utterances
cards.benefit_hypothesis: Different noncommutative evidence-composition paths may preserve high-order interactions without dependence on enumeration order.

cards.title: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning with Differentiable Pooling
cards.paper_read: https://www-cs.stanford.edu/~jure/pubs/diffpool-neurips18.pdf; section3.2, X'=S^T Z and A'=S^T A S
cards.code_provenance: Author SoftPoolingGcnEncoder.forward lines329-366 performs joint feature/adjacency coarsening and further graph propagation. loss lines368-400 explicitly makes link prediction conditional on self.linkpred; the forward mechanism does not require adding it.
computation_graph: Use real head tokens and fixed role/head graph: connect Local to every history head, same-role heads to each other and same-head nodes across roles. Add self loops only for graph convolution.
Separate graph encoders produce Z=GNN_embed(A,X) and S=softmax(GNN_assign(A,X)) with four cluster columns. Compute X1=S^T Z and A1=S^T A S; no post-hoc hand-made cluster adjacency.
Propagate on (A1,X1), then repeat assignment/coarsening to two clusters and propagate again. Preserve both assignment matrices.

Map coarse states back using S1 S2 and concatenate fine and first-level states before a linear zero residual bridge. This synthesis is an explicit OSRAM adapter, not part of the original graph classifier.
cards.substantive_difference: The learned adjacency itself is coarsened and drives the next graph stage. GMT/TokenLearner compress features via seeds/tokens without S^T A S graph hierarchy; ToMe merges selected pairs rather than assigning all nodes to jointly learned soft clusters. Only S-pooling without the coarsened-graph stage would fail the novelty requirement.
cards.mask_empty: Compact before graph encoding; inactive assignment rows do not exist. Coarsened cluster mass is derived only from valid nodes; safe degree floors handle low-mass clusters. Outer empty-history bypass exact.
cards.risk: No link-prediction or entropy auxiliary loss: assignment collapse is possible and original training recipe is not reproduced. Replace batch-coupled normalization by per-token LayerNorm as a declared adaptation. Small input graphs do not imply speed gain. Soft unpooling cannot reconstruct missing modalities.
mechanism_checks: Assignments sum to one per valid node
Coarsened adjacency symmetric for symmetric A
Two successive coarsening stages actually influence output
Inactive nodes cannot alter cluster mass or degrees
cards.benefit_hypothesis: Learning which evidence neighborhoods should be processed together at multiple graph scales may organize redundant and complementary heads.

cards.title: Weisfeiler and Lehman Go Cellular: CW Networks
cards.paper_read: https://arxiv.org/html/2106.12575; sections2-4, boundary/upper adjacency, ring lifting, cellular message passing
cards.code_provenance: Paper directly links author repository. SparseCINConv constructs per-dimension cochain layers with boundary and upper-neighbor messages, separate updates and combination; source lines271-342 read.
computation_graph: Create the typed Local/role/head graph used above. Lift every triangle and induced four-cycle into a 2-cell, retaining the complete edge boundary; cycle order is graph incidence, not time/head index adjacency.
Initialize vertex states from evidence, edge states from endpoint identities/content, and ring states from boundary-edge aggregates. Higher cells are current-forward tensors only.

Run three synchronous SparseCIN-style stages on dimensions0/1/2: aggregate boundary states; aggregate same-dimension upper neighbors conditioned on their shared coface; apply separate updates then combine. Read final vertex states plus incident edge/ring summaries to each original token.
Zero residual bridge returns only original Local/history coordinates. Use per-cell LayerNorm rather than batch normalization; no topology supervision.
cards.substantive_difference: Maintains distinct vertex/edge/closed-cycle states and boundary-of-boundary incidence. AllSet/ED-HNN exchange node and undifferentiated hyperedge states; Sheaf learns restrictions over incidence; PPGN composes arbitrary ordered pairs. Here edge-ring boundaries govern upper-neighbor communication; replacing cycles with generic set pools would erase the core.
cards.mask_empty: Build the induced complex only from valid vertices: delete every edge/cell whose vertices are absent. A cell must retain all its boundary faces. Empty cell dimensions use zero aggregate, not fake rings. Outer no-history bypass.
cards.risk: Cycles in a designed role/head graph are not chemical rings or observed semantic relations. Triangle/four-cycle count can be high; enumerate templates per legal mask once and profile tensor cost. Discrete topology depends only on allowed identities/mask, not test labels. Source expressivity claims do not transfer automatically to this finite designed topology.
mechanism_checks: Every cell boundary references only present faces
Induced four-cycles have no chord
Permutation of identity-bearing nodes preserves scattered result
Final edge/ring channels have task-gradient paths
cards.benefit_hypothesis: Closed multi-evidence relations may be easier to express using explicit edge and cycle states than vertex-only propagation.

cards.title: Simplicial Neural Networks
cards.paper_read: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.03633; Hodge Laplacian and local polynomial convolution on p-cochains
cards.code_provenance: Author repository linked from paper. SimplicialConvolution, Coboundary and Chebyshev recurrence read. Source experiments include imputation, but no source imputation objective or decoder is transferred.
computation_graph: Use the valid typed head graph and fill its triangles to make a two-dimensional simplicial complex. Choose a deterministic orientation from role/head identity solely to represent incidence matrices B1 and B2, verifying B1 B2=0.
Initialize edge cochains with an antisymmetric nonlinear endpoint encoder f(x_i,x_j)-f(x_j,x_i). Do not use only B1^T x: an exact gradient field can remove the curl-sensitive branch by construction.

Use L1=B1^T B1+B2 B2^T, normalize its spectrum safely, and apply three bias-free Chebyshev convolution/tanh stages to edge cochains. Odd activations preserve sign response under orientation flips. Vertex and triangle cochains can exchange states through the source Coboundary operators with their adjoints.

Read divergence B1 E and orientation-invariant incident |E| summaries to vertex tokens, concatenate original token states and zero-bridge write back. This lifting/readout is a declared evidence adaptation.
cards.substantive_difference: A signed cochain signal lives on edges and is transported through upper/lower Hodge incidence, with orientation-equivariant nonlinear stages. CWN uses nonlinear boundary/upper adjacency messages over cells; BernNet/scattering use vertex graph spectra; old Sheaf uses learned restriction maps. Keeping only vertex Laplacian polynomial filtering would make this candidate redundant and is disallowed.
cards.mask_empty: Remove every inactive incident simplex and reconstruct incidence on the resulting subcomplex. Empty triangle set means a zero-width B2 and L1=B1^T B1; no invented simplex. No-history bypass exact.
cards.risk: Evidence differences are not observed physical flows. Orientation must not become semantic ordering. Bias or nonodd activations can violate the chosen orientation contract. Nonlinear edge initialization and edge readout must remain present; otherwise the mechanism can collapse to a vertex graph filter. No imputation of absent modalities is authorized.
mechanism_checks: B1 B2 exactly zero
Flip arbitrary edge orientations and transform B1/B2/E consistently; vertex output unchanged
Nonzero curl-sensitive response for constructed synthetic edge field
Finite spectral normalization for empty/zero Laplacian
cards.benefit_hypothesis: Separating relation signals carried by boundaries and closed evidence cycles may expose structure missed by vertex-only mixing.

cards.title: Nested Graph Neural Networks
cards.paper_read: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.13197; rooted induced subgraphs and inner/outer graph representation
cards.code_provenance: Author repository; create_subgraphs retains induced edges and node-to-subgraph mapping; NestedGIN encodes all copies then pools inside and across subgraphs. Both source sections read.
computation_graph: Build typed head graph from active tokens. For every original token extract its one-hop induced subgraph including all edges between neighbors; mark the root and shortest-hop distance explicitly.
Replicate original features into their subgraph copies, concatenate root/distance embeddings, and execute a shared three-layer GIN over disconnected subgraph copies with per-token LayerNorm.

Pool multi-layer states within each subgraph to produce a representation for its original root, then combine root features with pooled whole-graph context for the zero residual bridge. Every original token obtains its own rooted-subgraph result.
cards.substantive_difference: A node has multiple separately evolving copies conditioned on different roots; induced edges among its neighbors are retained before inner computation. Existing message passing has one state per node and a rooted computation tree, while PPGN has a pair tensor with matrix products. This is not replacing a graph convolution or increasing hop count.
cards.mask_empty: Extract subgraphs after compacting valid tokens, retaining only induced edges. Never let absent nodes form paths or change hop labels. Isolated root subgraph is valid; external no-history bypass.
cards.risk: Local connects to every history node, so its rooted subgraph is the full evidence graph; other roots must retain genuinely smaller induced neighborhoods or this becomes mostly duplicate computation. Designed topology changes only with mask. Source WL results do not prove a useful MOSI signal. Extra copies cost roughly O(n times local edges).
mechanism_checks: Each subgraph contains its marked root
Edges are induced, not just a BFS tree
Different roots keep independent intermediate states
Scatter back respects original token identity
cards.benefit_hypothesis: Receiver-specific induced-neighborhood computation may represent contextual evidence configurations more explicitly than shared global node states.

cards.title: Graph U-Nets
cards.paper_read: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/gao19a/gao19a.pdf; sections3.1-3.3, node selection, graph augmentation and indexed unpool
cards.code_provenance: Author GraphUnet/Pool/Unpool/top_k_graph read in full. Source pools sigmoid linear scores, augments adjacency by its Boolean square, saves indices and restores zero-filled slots before upward graph convolutions and skip addition.
computation_graph: Encode valid evidence head graph. Run two encoder graph-convolution stages, each followed by learned normalized projection score, sigmoid weighting and top-k selection with fixed ratio0.5 and k clipped to the valid node count.

Before selection augment the graph with two-hop connectivity using the Boolean square of A+I, then retain the selected induced graph. Save each selected-index map and pre-pool feature/adjacency tensors.

Run a bottom graph convolution; decode in reverse order by zero-scattering selected states to the saved node indices, graph-convolving on the saved adjacency, and adding the corresponding pre-pool skip. Decode all original valid tokens through the zero residual bridge.
cards.substantive_difference: Hierarchical hard node selection plus connectivity augmentation, index-preserving unpool and graph decoder is distinct from DiffPool soft S^T A S, ToMe pairwise merging and FSPool per-channel ranking. A scalar gate/top-k by itself is expressly not the candidate.
cards.mask_empty: Only valid compact nodes can be ranked. k=min(n,max(1,floor(0.5*n))) prevents source max(2,...) from exceeding tiny n. Missing/unselected nodes get zero bottom-up state but preserved encoder skip; nonexistent OSRAM roles remain zero. Outer no-history bypass.
cards.risk: Selection changes discontinuously and unselected ranking entries lack direct top-k gradients. Source code differs from paper in score normalization and uses potentially ambiguous broadcast degree normalization: implement the declared paper normalized projection and explicit row degree shape rather than silently inheriting this. Decoder unpool restores indexing, not lost information or missing modalities.
mechanism_checks: Selected indices valid and unique at each level
Unpool exactly restores the selected positions
Encoder skips carry all retained original valid nodes
Top-k boundary gradients described honestly; gradcheck only away from ties
cards.benefit_hypothesis: A coarse evidence bottleneck with explicit fine-resolution bypasses may suppress distracting heads while retaining individual evidence context.

cards.title: Conditional Random Fields as Recurrent Neural Networks
cards.paper_read: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1502.03240; Gaussian pairwise CRF and unrolled mean-field stages
cards.code_provenance: Original torrvision/crfasrnn repository links this author-maintained PyTorch version. CrfRnn source read in full: softmax, two filtering branches, kernel weights, compatibility transform and unary reinjection. It is a 2019 author port, not the original 2015 Caffe implementation.
computation_graph: Project each current evidence token to K=8 latent-state unary logits U_i and a separate content-kernel descriptor f_i. These internal states are not the emotion classes or a new supervised head.

Construct two symmetric off-diagonal kernels exactly on the small valid set: one Gaussian on content descriptors; one Gaussian on fixed role/head identity descriptors. Identity descriptors are categorical, not artificial pixel positions or time coordinates. Combine with learned scalar kernel weights and a learned symmetric KxK compatibility matrix.

Initialize Q=softmax(U). Perform five shared mean-field steps: M_i(l)=sum_m w_m sum_{j != i} k_m(i,j) Q_j(l); Q_i=softmax(U_i-C M_i). Unary U remains the original unary at every step, not recurrently overwritten.

Decode concatenated unary posterior, final posterior and their difference together with the original token into corrections. Keep only existing task loss; no CRF NLL, pseudo labels, pairwise labels or segmentation objective.
cards.substantive_difference: The block performs approximate inference in a discrete pairwise latent-state Gibbs model with compatibility between state labels and persistent unary terms. RAT-SPN uses decomposable sum-product circuits; capsules infer mixture assignment/posteriors; RRN learns free recurrent messages; DEQ solves a continuous equilibrium. No external convergence/implicit solver is substituted.
cards.mask_empty: Compact before kernel normalization. Remove self interactions explicitly; no absent node can contribute to pairwise mass. No-history bypass; one-token core keeps its unary distribution at every step.
cards.risk: Kernel feature geometry and latent states are task-learned, not calibrated uncertainty or known labels. Gaussian image filters are replaced by exact set kernels and compatibility is symmetrized, so this is a CRF-RNN inference-core adaptation, not full segmentation model reproduction. Mean-field may oscillate or over-smooth; finite five steps does not imply convergence. Author code uses a plus-sign compatibility convention; chosen minus-energy convention must be consistent throughout.
mechanism_checks: Each Q row sums to one
Zero pairwise weights return unary Q exactly
One-token result equals unary
Manual one-step mean-field matches code and sign convention
No gold label is accepted by forward
cards.benefit_hypothesis: Pairwise compatibility between latent evidence interpretations may resolve inconsistent token assignments through joint inference.

cards.title: Graph Matching Networks for Learning the Similarity of Graph Structured Objects
cards.code_provenance: Author DeepMind notebook re-read directly: GraphPropLayer, compute_cross_attention, batch_block_pair_attention, GraphPropMatchingLayer and GraphMatchingNet. GraphPropMatchingLayer explicitly combines within-graph messages with node_states minus cross-graph attention; GRU is an available source update type.
cards.previous_status: experiments/osram_readout20_reconsidered_20261003/set_reasoning.json graph_matching_network was REJECT_CURRENT_CONTRACT. Reasons: singleton Local-vs-history degenerates, meaningful two-graph pairing absent, Gap can be empty, and source similarity losses forbidden.
cards.resolution: Do not use singleton Local as a graph. For each active Gap form a pair of full eight-head graphs: Base8 is shared-history readout and Gap8 is modality-missing-specific history readout from the same OSRAM head layout. Same-head identity supports a declared correspondence hypothesis. Local conditions both encoders. If no Gap is active return identity. Only the pairwise interaction block transfers; no graph-similarity task/loss. Old rejection remains valid for the earlier singleton construction.
computation_graph: For each active modality Gap, project Base's eight real heads and that Gap's eight real heads separately to two eight-node graphs, adding matching head identity and Local condition. Use complete nonself edges within each head graph, with edge identity features indicating equal/different head semantics as appropriate; do not impose head sequence neighbors.

For four shared propagation rounds compute learned within-graph endpoint messages and sum them at receivers. Simultaneously compute both directions of cross-graph softmax matching from the same old states.
For each node form mismatch delta=h_i-sum_j a_ij h_j from the opposite graph and feed [within_message,delta,Local_condition] into a shared GRU node update. Both graphs update synchronously.

Decode each Gap correction from its pair's final nodes. Average Base corrections over active Gap pairs before writing Base once; Local remains unchanged. All graphs and GRU states reset each utterance.
cards.substantive_difference: Full within-graph relation propagation and bidirectional cross-graph mismatch jointly update both node systems. DCN co-attends directly with additive transforms; MCAN has asymmetric self/cross stages; Hyper-SAGNN compares static and leave-self-out representations inside a hyperedge, not two coupled graph systems. Merely subtracting one attention vector without internal graph propagation would be rejected.
cards.mask_empty: Only construct pairs for actually active Gap roles and valid prior history. Both members then contain the genuine eight heads. With zero active Gap return original Base/Local and zero inactive Gap correction exactly; no learned null graph. Average Base updates only by the actual active pair count.
cards.risk: Shared vs gap history are not observed isomorphic objects and matched heads may still carry different semantics. Complete internal graphs are a modeling choice. Source pair/triplet retrieval training is omitted; only existing task gradients supervise the interaction core. This candidate does nothing at fully observed rate0, by design, and must not be advertised as a generic all-rate architecture change.
mechanism_checks: All-observed case is exact identity
One/two active Gap pairs both finite
Base correction uses actual active pair count
Update graphs synchronously from old state
Within-message and mismatch branches both have task-gradient paths
cards.benefit_hypothesis: Jointly comparing common and missingness-specific history graphs may preserve differences that direct averaging or independent co-attention misses.

not_counted.name: DPP
not_counted.reason: Already among root's nine retained candidates; do not count twice.

not_counted.name: Dempster-Shafer prototype layer
not_counted.reason: Owned by representation lane; earlier source-formula mismatch must be resolved there.

not_counted.name: GSN subgraph counts
not_counted.reason: On the proposed fixed role/head topology counts are deterministic from availability and identity. Adding them to ordinary message passing would be a weak wrapper, not enough for this quota.

not_counted.name: DSS
not_counted.reason: No justified additional within-element symmetry in fixed learned coordinates; avoid artificially treating channels as interchangeable.

not_counted.name: SAGPool alone
not_counted.reason: A node scoring gate and top-k plus ordinary GNN is too small; Graph U-Net is retained only with the complete down/up hierarchy.

not_counted.name: EM Matrix Capsules
not_counted.reason: Existing Variational Bayes capsule routing already covers Gaussian vote-responsibility inference; no extra count without a stronger nonoverlap case.

not_counted.name: Set2Set
not_counted.reason: Potentially too close to existing MAC recurrent readout for present quota; not pursued as a filler.
